newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-OTTAWA RALLIES TO BEAT CANADIENS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-OTTAWA RALLIES TO BEAT CANADIENS.

text.p: Alexandre Daigle and Alexei Yashin each had two goals and an assist as the Ottawa Senators rallied from a three-goal deficit Saturday to defeat the Montreal Canadiens 6-3.
Montreal scored on its first three shots of the game, but goalie Damian Rhodes stopped the final 21 as Ottawa improved to 2-1-3, the best start in the team's five-year history.
"I was fighting the puck in the first period and I was wondering how my reflexes were," Rhodes said. "This afternoon, my trainer gave me a reflex test and said I was a little bit slow.

"When the Canadiens took a 3-0 lead and I didn't look too good, I was beginning to think he was right. Early in the second, I made a big save on (Saku) Koivu, which helped my confidence. And with the crowd behind me, my confidence grew and things fell into place the rest of the night."

Daigle's power-play goal with 5:14 left in the second period lifted the Senators into a 3-3 tie. He scored again on a breakaway at 5:01 of the third to put Ottawa ahead to stay. Shawn McEachern made it 5-3 just over five minutes later.
Daniel Alfredsson contributed three assists for Ottawa, which has rallied from third-period deficits for two wins and two ties.
In Pittsburgh, Ron Francis's goal snapped a second-period tie and Ken Wregget made 18 saves as the Penguins edged the Washington Capitals 2-1 in a battle of struggling teams.
With the score tied, Francis took a pass from Alek Stojanov at the top of the right circle, skated down the right side and cut across the crease, beating goaltender Jim Carey on the stick side.

Wregget stopped 10 shots in the first period, but only eight the rest of the way as the Penguins won for the second time in seven games this season. Washington has lost three straight and five of its first six games.
In Dallas, Andy Moog stopped 14 shots for his first shutout of the season and Dave Reid and Greg Adams scored as the Dallas Stars blanked the Toronto Maple Leafs 2-0.

Moog, the league's oldest active netminder at 36, stopped three shots in the first period, four in the second and seven in the third and was never really tested. The shutout was the 23rd of his 16-year career.
Toronto's Felix Potvin made 23 saves as the Maple Leafs dropped their fifth straight after winning their opener.
At Colorado, Scott Young and Joe Sakic each had two goals and an assist as the Colorado Avalanche crushed the Vancouver Canucks 9-2.
The Avalanche, 4-1-1 since losing their first two games of the season, broke open a scoreless game with four goals in the second period.
Patrick Roy was closing in on a league-leading third shutout of the season until Pavel Bure scored with 2:17 left.

In Hartford, Andrew Cassels, Jeff O'Neill and Marek Malik scored in a 2:22 span of the first period and Keith Primeau added his first two goals as a Whaler, leading Hartford to its fourth win in five games, 6-2 over the New Jersey Devils.
Jason Muzzatti made 34 saves for the Whalers, who broke a four-game home winless streak against New Jersey.
In Detroit, Viacheslav Fetisov scored with 1:01 left in the second period to snap a tie and lift the Detroit Red Wings to a 4-2 victory over the New York Islanders.
Fetisov was in the slot when he took a centering pass from Brendan Shanahan and put a wrist shot past goaltender Tommy Salo as he was being dragged down by Islanders winger Niklas Andersson.
The Red Wings, who were second in the Western Conference with 325 goals last season, scored more than three goals for just the second time in seven games this season.
